name: Die Cut Decals
seoTitle: Die Cut Decals: Custom Cut Vinyl Decals for Cars & Windows
seoDescription: Custom die cut decals in cut vinyl or printed, laminated vinyl, trimmed to your artwork outline for vehicles, storefront glass and walls. Free proof.
tagline: Vinyl graphics cut to your outline, pre-masked and ready to apply to glass, paint and walls.
quickAnswer: Die cut decals are vinyl graphics cut to the exact outline of your artwork, supplied either as single-color cut vinyl with transfer tape or as full-color printed, laminated vinyl that is contour cut. They suit fleet lettering, storefront glass, wall graphics and boat numbers. Sizes run from 0.5 inch lettering to 24 by 36 inch panels, from $0.30 each with a 100 piece minimum, produced in 5 to 7 business days after proof approval.
highlights: Material: cut vinyl or printed laminated vinyl

sections.h2: Decals or stickers: what you are actually ordering
sections.html:
Ask three sign shops for a die cut decal and you may get three different products, so here is how we define it. A die cut decal is a vinyl graphic cut to the outline of your artwork with no background around it. We build them two ways. The first is cut vinyl: a single-color film (white, black, a standard color or a Pantone match) with the letters or shapes cut out and weeded, then pre-masked with transfer tape so a whole word goes onto the surface in one move. The second is printed vinyl: full-color artwork printed, laminated, then contour cut, which is what most buyers want for a logo on a van door or a window.

The nearest sibling is our die cut vinyl sticker. Those are printed pieces on a paper backing, usually 2 to 6 inches, handed out at events or stuck on laptops and bottles. Decals are the bigger, more permanent cousin: hours of business on a glass door, fleet graphics, gym wall art, registration numbers on a boat. If you are still deciding which format fits, our guide to stickers, decals and labels walks through the differences with examples.

sections.h2: Surfaces where cut vinyl decals hold up
sections.html:
Cut vinyl has no ink layer to scratch, so on a smooth surface it usually outlasts a printed piece. Our calendered vinyl typically gives three to five years outdoors on a vertical surface and longer indoors. It bonds well to:

  • Storefront glass, applied to the outside face or reverse cut for mounting inside the window
  • Factory paint on vehicle doors, tailgates and hoods, once wax has been wiped off with alcohol
  • Painted drywall in offices, gyms and studios, where a removable adhesive protects the paint later
  • Fiberglass and gelcoat on boats, trailers and RVs
  • Powder-coated metal on toolboxes, signs and equipment
  • Acrylic and polycarbonate panels on trade show displays

Avoid textured stucco, brick, unsealed wood and silicone-treated plastics. The vinyl sticks at first and lifts within a week. Also skip lettering under about 0.25 inches tall; the weeding step tears it. If your project is more of a short-run handout than a fixed graphic, the sticker range on our homepage is the better starting point.

sections.h2: Which decal build fits the job
sections.html:
Most decal problems come from choosing the wrong build rather than the wrong color. Use this table to match the construction to the surface and the time it needs to last.

Printed and laminatedWhite vinyl, gloss or matte laminateTypically 3 to 5 yearsFull-color logos on vans, trailers and signs

Printed decals carry a laminate as standard because the ink sits on top of the film and needs a shield from sun and car-wash brushes. Cut vinyl does not need one. For a window seen from both sides, order two mirrored pieces rather than one clear piece; the color looks richer.

sections.h2: Applying a transfer-tape decal without bubbles
sections.html:
Decals arrive as three layers: backing paper, the vinyl, and transfer tape on top. Work in the shade between about 50 and 90 degrees Fahrenheit and follow this order.

  1. Clean the surface with isopropyl alcohol on a lint-free cloth and let it flash off. Skip glass cleaner; the ammonia leaves a film.
  2. Position the decal with the backing still on and mark the top corners with masking tape.
  3. Lay a strip of masking tape across the top edge as a hinge.
  4. Lift the decal from the bottom, peel the backing away from the vinyl, and cut it off a few inches from the hinge.
  5. Squeegee from the hinge downward in overlapping strokes, pressing firmly, so air pushes out ahead of the vinyl.
  6. Peel the transfer tape back on itself at a sharp angle, slowly. If a letter lifts, lay the tape back down and squeegee that spot again.
  7. Leave it alone for 24 hours before washing or exposing it to rain.

Small bubbles under a printed decal usually work out in a few sunny days. On cut vinyl, prick them with a pin and press flat.

sections.h2: Artwork rules that save a reprint
sections.html:
Cut vinyl needs vector outlines: AI, EPS, SVG or a vector PDF with fonts converted to outlines. A JPG cannot drive a plotter. Keep every stroke at least 0.1 inch wide and every gap between shapes at least 0.06 inch, or the plotter will not separate them cleanly. Printed decals accept a 300 dpi PNG or JPG at final size, though vector still gives the cleanest cut line.

Single pieces go up to 24 by 36 inches. Anything larger ships as tiled panels with a 0.5 inch overlap marked on the proof. Your free digital proof shows the cut path in magenta so you can check that counters inside letters and thin tails will survive. Small printed pieces for jars and boxes belong on our custom die cut labels page, which uses paper and BOPP stocks rather than sign vinyl.

sections.h2: Quantities, timing and what arrives in the box
sections.html:
The minimum is 100 decals per design, and a mix of sizes of the same artwork counts toward it. Production takes 5 to 7 business days after you approve the proof, with delivery inside 8 to 10 business days by FedEx, free anywhere in the United States. Rush runs are available if you tell us the date on the quote request.

Cut vinyl arrives fully weeded and masked, stacked flat with a backing sheet between every ten pieces. Printed decals come laminated and trimmed, flat up to 18 inches and rolled above that. Check the count and the color against your proof when the box lands; defective decals are reprinted at no charge within our 10 day return window.

faqs.q: Are die cut decals the same as die cut vinyl stickers?
faqs.a: No. A die cut decal is a cut vinyl or printed vinyl graphic meant for a fixed surface such as a window, vehicle or wall, often applied with transfer tape. Die cut vinyl stickers are smaller printed pieces on a backing that you peel and press by hand, usually for laptops, bottles and handouts.

faqs.q: Can die cut decals be made in one color without any printing?
faqs.a: Yes. Single-color decals are cut from solid vinyl film, so there is no ink to fade or scratch. We stock standard colors and can match a Pantone reference. This is the right choice for lettering, hours of business, phone numbers and simple logos, and it typically lasts longer outdoors than a printed piece.

faqs.q: Will cut vinyl decals come off my storefront glass cleanly?
faqs.a: Yes, with a little heat. Warm the vinyl with a hair dryer, lift a corner with a plastic razor and peel at a low angle. Any adhesive left behind wipes off with isopropyl alcohol or a citrus remover. Glass is the easiest surface to clean up because nothing soaks into it.

faqs.q: How big can a single die cut decal be?
faqs.a: One piece goes up to 24 by 36 inches. Larger graphics are split into panels with a half-inch overlap, and the proof shows where each seam falls so you can keep it away from faces and text. Most van door logos sit between 12 and 24 inches wide.

faqs.q: Do you supply die cut decals with transfer tape already applied?
faqs.a: Yes. Every cut vinyl decal ships weeded and pre-masked with transfer tape, so a word of separate letters stays in alignment while you apply it. Printed and contour cut decals do not need tape because the piece is one solid shape; you peel it from the backing and squeegee it down.

faqs.q: Can die cut decals go through a car wash?
faqs.a: Yes, after a 72 hour cure. Both cut vinyl and laminated printed decals handle brush and touchless washes. Avoid pointing a pressure washer directly at the edges from closer than about a foot, since a high-pressure jet can lift a corner that then collects dirt.

faqs.q: What file do I need to send for a cut vinyl decal?
faqs.a: A vector file: AI, EPS, SVG or a PDF saved from a vector program, with all text converted to outlines. The plotter follows the vector path, so a PNG or JPG cannot be used. If you only have a raster logo, our design team can redraw it as vector before the proof at no charge.

faqs.q: Can I get die cut decals in a Pantone color?
faqs.a: Yes. For cut vinyl we select the closest film from the manufacturer's color range and note the match on the proof. For printed decals we mix to the Pantone reference in CMYK. Solid colors on cut film are the more exact of the two, which matters for strict brand guidelines.

faqs.q: Do die cut decals work on painted interior walls?
faqs.a: Yes, on smooth, fully cured paint. We use a removable adhesive for wall decals so they come off without pulling the finish. Wait at least two weeks after painting before applying, and avoid textured, matte washable paints with additives, which stop the vinyl from bonding.

faqs.q: How many die cut decals do I have to order?
faqs.a: The minimum is 100 decals per design. If you need the same logo in several sizes, the sizes count together toward the 100. Pricing starts from $0.30 per piece and depends on the size, material and quantity, so a quote with your dimensions gives the exact figure.

faqs.q: How long do custom die cut decals take to make and ship?
faqs.a: Production takes 5 to 7 business days once you approve the free digital proof, and FedEx delivery brings the total to 8 to 10 business days anywhere in the United States. Shipping is free. If you have a hard deadline for a fleet rollout or an opening, ask about rush production when you request the quote.

faqs.q: Can a die cut decal be reverse cut for the inside of a window?
faqs.a: Yes. We mirror the artwork and cut it so the adhesive faces outward, which lets you apply the decal on the inside of the glass where weather and vandals cannot reach it. Reverse cut works for cut vinyl and for printed clear decals with a white ink layer behind the color.
